title: ADJECTIVES & ADVERBS
notes:
✓ Adjective → A word that describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun.

◆ Examples
She is a careful student.
The exam was difficult.

✓ Adverb → A word that describes a verb, an adjective, another adverb, or sometimes a whole sentence.

◆ Examples
She studies carefully.
The exam was extremely difficult.
He runs very quickly.

✓ Quick rule → Adjective describes a noun/pronoun; adverb usually describes how, when, where, or to what degree something happens.

title: ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Adjectives commonly describe:

◆ People → kind, intelligent, honest
◆ Things → large, expensive, beautiful
◆ Places → peaceful, crowded, modern
◆ Ideas/situations → difficult, important, interesting

◆ Examples
She bought a beautiful dress.
He is an intelligent student.
Addis Ababa is a busy city.

title: POSITION OF ADJECTIVES
notes:
✓ Adjectives commonly appear:

◆ Before a noun → a beautiful house.

◆ After linking verbs → The house is beautiful.

✓ Common linking verbs → be, seem, become, feel, look, appear, sound, smell, taste.

◆ Examples
She looks tired.
The food tastes delicious.
He became angry.

✓ After linking verbs, use an adjective, not an adverb.

❌ The food tastes deliciously.
✓ The food tastes delicious.

title: ADVERBS
notes:
✓ Adverbs give information about:

◆ Manner → how?
She speaks slowly.

◆ Time → when?
He arrived yesterday.

◆ Place → where?
Come here.

◆ Frequency → how often?
She always studies.

◆ Degree → how much/to what extent?
He is very tired.

✓ Adverbs make the meaning of actions and descriptions more precise.

title: ADVERBS OF MANNER
notes:
✓ Adverbs of manner → Describe how an action happens.

◆ Examples
slowly
carefully
quickly
quietly
beautifully
easily
seriously

◆ Sentences
She answered carefully.
He drove quickly.
They worked quietly.

✓ Many adverbs of manner are formed with adjective + -ly.

title: ADJECTIVE → ADVERB
notes:
✓ Common formation:

careful → carefully
slow → slowly
quick → quickly
beautiful → beautifully
quiet → quietly
serious → seriously

✓ Adjectives ending in consonant + y:
happy → happily
easy → easily
angry → angrily

✓ Adjectives ending in -le often change to -ly:
simple → simply
gentle → gently

✓ Spelling changes must be remembered.

title: ADJECTIVES THAT DO NOT FOLLOW -LY
notes:
✓ Some common adverbs do not simply follow adjective + -ly.

◆ Common forms
good → well
fast → fast
hard → hard
late → late
early → early

◆ Examples
She is a good singer.
She sings well.

He is a fast runner.
He runs fast.

He is a hard worker.
He works hard.

title: HARD / HARDLY & LATE / LATELY
notes:
✓ Hard → With great effort.
He works hard.

✓ Hardly → Almost not.
He hardly works. → He works very little/almost not at all.

✓ Late → After the expected time.
He arrived late.

✓ Lately → Recently.
I haven't seen him lately.

✓ The -ly form can have a completely different meaning.

title: POSITION OF ADVERBS
notes:
✓ Adverb position depends on its type.

◆ Manner → Often after the verb/object.
She spoke quietly.

◆ Frequency → Usually before the main verb.
She always studies.

◆ Frequency with be → After be.
She is always punctual.

◆ Degree → Usually before the adjective/adverb.
He is very intelligent.

✓ Position can change for emphasis, but these are the common patterns.

title: ADVERBS OF FREQUENCY
notes:
✓ Common frequency adverbs:

100% → always
80–90% → usually/normally
60–70% → often/frequently
40–50% → sometimes
10–20% → rarely/seldom
0% → never

◆ Examples
I always study at night.
She usually arrives early.
He often plays football.
They sometimes eat outside.
We rarely watch television.
He never smokes.

✓ Main verb → Adverb usually comes before it.
✓ Be → Adverb usually comes after it.

title: ADVERBS OF DEGREE
notes:
✓ Adverbs of degree → Show intensity or amount.

very → very difficult
really → really important
extremely → extremely expensive
quite → quite easy
too → too difficult
enough → good enough

◆ Examples
The question is very difficult.
She runs extremely quickly.
He is too tired to work.
The room is warm enough.

title: ADJECTIVE OR ADVERB?
notes:
✓ Compare the function, not just the spelling.

She is a careful driver. → adjective + noun.
She drives carefully. → adverb + verb.

He is a slow runner. → adjective.
He runs slowly. → adverb.

She is a good singer. → adjective.
She sings well. → adverb.

✓ Ask → Is the word describing a noun/person, or is it describing an action?

title: COMMON ADJECTIVE/ADVERB ERRORS
notes:
❌ She sings beautiful.
✓ She sings beautifully.

❌ He drives dangerous.
✓ He drives dangerously.

❌ She speaks English fluent.
✓ She speaks English fluently.

❌ He did the work careful.
✓ He did the work carefully.

❌ She feels happily.
✓ She feels happy.

❌ The food tastes well.
✓ The food tastes good.

✓ Action verb → Often needs an adverb.
✓ Linking verb → Normally takes an adjective.

title: SPECIAL -LY WORDS
notes:
✓ Not every word ending in -ly is an adverb.

◆ Examples
friendly → adjective
lovely → adjective
lonely → adjective
lively → adjective
likely → adjective

She is friendly.

❌ She behaved friendly.
✓ She behaved in a friendly way.

✓ Do not identify a word as an adverb only because it ends in -ly.

title: QUICK EXAM GUIDE
notes:
◆ 1. Find the word being described.

◆ 2. If it describes a noun/pronoun → adjective.

◆ 3. If it describes an action/verb → usually adverb.

◆ 4. After linking verbs → usually adjective.
She looks tired.

◆ 5. Many manner adverbs → adjective + -ly.
careful → carefully.

◆ 6. Remember irregular/common forms:
good → well
fast → fast
hard → hard
early → early
late → late

◆ 7. Watch meaning-changing pairs:
hard ≠ hardly
late ≠ lately

✓ Golden rule → Adjective describes a person, thing, or noun; adverb mainly describes an action, adjective, or another adverb.
